reader.requirement: At --std 85 LOG's argument-1 value must be greater than zero; for a positive value the natural logarithm is returned, and for a value not greater than zero the result of the reference is undefined (§1989:A.2.2 AR4), so the compiler must evaluate positive arguments correctly and may do anything defined-or-not for others (1985 has no exception condition to raise).

edition-consulted.switches: sig.IntroducedIn > ctx.Edition.DialectLevel refuses a function not yet introduced (DiagnosticCatalog.IntrinsicFunctionNotYetIntroduced); the 1989 functions carry IntroducedIn 85 in IntrinsicCatalog, so --std 85 admits them

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectBehavior|CobolVersion over IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFloat/DomainArg, RuntimeApi.cs#DomainArg and CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Log: none; the domain screen (IntrinsicDomain.Positive in IntrinsicCatalog) and the NaN-to-EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION raise in RealResult are the same at every edition, and EC checking is off unless enabled (1985 has no >>TURN)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: LOG(0)/LOG10(-1) store 0 at both --std 85 and --std 2023 with checking off
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf39_01 covers positive arguments only; the out-of-range half (undefined) is not exercised

probes.expected: natural logarithm of each positive argument (A.2.20.4 RV1)

probes.printed: --std 85 and --std 2023 alike: exit 0; LOG(0) and LOG10(-1) store 0000.000000 (no SIZE ERROR), LOG(M1+2)=0; log-lit0.cob (LOG(0), LOG10(-5) literals on an unexecuted branch) compiles and runs, prints NOT-REFERENCED-OK
probes.expected: a value not greater than zero is outside the permissible range: the result of the reference is undefined (§1989:A.2.2 AR4), so any value conforms; a positive argument gives the logarithm

reader.notes: The positive half is exact to the 6 places probed (ln 300, ln 100, ln 5). Zero and negative arguments leave execution running with result 0, which the 1985 text permits as an undefined result; a literal 0 on an unexecuted branch is not refused, which is right since the rule constrains the value at reference time.

refuter.evidence: Rule: value must be greater than zero; otherwise §1989:A.2.2 says the result of the reference is undefined, so only the positive range is constrained. Probed the positive extremes the reader skipped: logext-002 LOG(1E-18 via PIC SV9(18))=-41.446531, LOG(999999999999999999)=41.446531, LOG(e to 18 digits)=1.000000, all correct to 6 places; reader's log-domain probe shows nonpositive values run to completion (undefined result permitted). No compile-time refusal of LOG(0) exists, which is right since the constraint is on the value at reference. cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.20.3 AR2 the text is in AR2; OK §1989:A.2.2 the text is in the clause; it lies in AR4 (the 'then the result of such a reference is undefined' sentence follows item 4).
